'''def solve_fabric(profile, cal, fabric):
    """Exact envelope, peaks, guard selection, witness and warmup cycle.

    The envelope is the lexicographic (error allowance, elapsed age) minimum
    over all lineages from the anchor states, obtained by one Dijkstra per
    guard setting because transfer eligibility depends on the setting.  All
    step weights are nonnegative, so the minimum over walks is the minimum
    over simple lineages and every finite label is attained by an actual
    lineage; states that remain unreached are unknown.

    Reachability shrinks with the guard, so once a setting leaves some
    phase-device unknown every larger setting does too.  The warmup cycle is
    the smallest ``k`` with ``min_age(p, i) <= k*P + p`` for every phase-device:
    a lineage of that age started at boundary ``k*P + p - min_age`` is realisable
    from startup, and no optimal lineage ending at that boundary can be older
    than the boundary itself.
    """''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='para.py'; s=open(p).read()
s = s.replace('''def calibrate(profile):
    """Exact calibration artifact for a measurement profile."""''',
'''def calibrate(profile):
    """Exact calibration artifact for a measurement profile.

    Records are difference constraints ``x[b] - x[a] <= w``.  The profile is
    infeasible exactly when the constraint graph has a negative cycle, which
    Bellman-Ford from a virtual source detects and reports as a constraint-id
    cycle.  Otherwise the tight supremum of ``x[b] - x[a]`` is the shortest
    path distance from ``a`` to ``b``; Johnson potentials make the edges
    nonnegative so one Dijkstra per source yields the whole matrix together
    with a constraint-id shortest-path tree.  Row ``a`` of that matrix is a
    feasible bias vector with ``x[a] = 0``, which attains the supremum, while
    the reported predecessor chains bound it from above.
    """''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
